title: Head of the National AI Directorate (National Artificial Intelligence Headquarters), Prime Minister's Office; Brig. Gen. (res.)
company: Israel National AI Directorate (Prime Minister's Office)
top_signal: 9 Nov 2026, AI & Cyber Week, Tel Aviv University: Askal set a national target of about 300,000 GPUs tied to 2 GW. About 100k would serve academia, government, defence and startups, and 200k tech companies and data centres. He also called for an Israeli frontier model built with partner countries ('we do not have to build it alone'). RuntimeWire reports that the formal approved baseline is 100,000 accelerators and that 300k is an aspirational target. A separate report on the approved national AI plan says 5,000 top-end GPUs would be made accessible each year for 2027-2032. The current national system (Telem, built by Nebius) went live in Jan 2026 with 1,000 B200s.
confidence: Signal: medium (most coverage traces to one CTech/Calcalist report of the speech). Fit: low.
est_blocks: 2 (speculative; only if offshore capacity is acceptable)
why_now: The GPU-access targets start in 2027, the frontier-model ambition needs training capacity, and the 1,000-GPU Telem phase is small against the target. Export-control and data-residency: the plan's stated aim is domestic sovereign infrastructure, so Raion's UK/EU/US/Canada capacity probably fits only interim or overflow training or a partner-country frontier-model run. Before outreach, confirm whether government or defence data may leave Israel and whether US export licensing applies to an Israeli government user of US-sited Blackwell capacity. Purchases are likely to go through a public tender (Telem was tendered).
jan_2027_ready: no - targets start in 2027, no procurement or tender announced yet, and the data-residency fit is unresolved
